note: Ambient life routines for the living-world director (src/lib/livingWorld.ts): where each placed person (and creature citizen) is, per clock phase, and what their lines are. Routines are data, resolved against the clock design's five phases (LATE/MORN/DAY/EVE/NITE). An entry with present:false is the authored way of being somewhere else (home, indoors, off-post) — quiet is a phase of life, not missing content. Flag gates compose with the director's world state (event resolutions and arc completions set the flags named here). Creature citizens speak in cries only — their lines are renderings of sound, never words (canon). Positions are checked against the maps' walkable tiles at authoring time; the engine seam (see LANDING-RECORD) applies them.

lines: Pupbble: *contented yip, watching the water*
Pupbble: *contented yip, watching the water*
Pupbble: *curled up asleep against a crate, one ear up*
Mochii: *a bright chirp at everyone who passes the lab door*
Kittember: *tail-flame low and calm, curled against the herbalist's pack*
Kittember: *watching the west grass, flame lower than it should be*
Forty years on this harbour. Nine of them with her beside me.
You didn't see a runner, did you? Grey hood, fast feet?
Evening boats are all in. She's usually asleep against the crate by now.
Can't sleep right, knowing she's out there. Harbours are loud at night when you're listening for one sound.
There she is. Still can't quite believe it some mornings.
This harbour looks after its own. You taught it that.
Dinner's at dusk in this house. Wherever the road takes you — you have a table.
Technology is incredible! The lab's new terminal catalogues every creature anyone's ever SEEN.
Some day it'll know more than any of us. Some day soon, the way it's going.
Even the harbour slows down eventually. Even me.
Early is when you train. Remember that when you're still asleep.
Tomorrow I leave for real. Watch the harbour if you want a head start on missing me.
Again. From the top. A borrowed win doesn't count and we both know it.
He trains like the street is watching. Some mornings, it is.
Mending nets is just knots, all the way down. Like most honest work.
Harbour's best hour. Everything coming home, everything lit.
The Dojo rests. Even the Unbreakable Core sleeps — that IS the discipline.
The grass south of the cross path rustles different lately. Everyone's heard it.
Plex steps are the town's front porch at dusk. Everybody ends up here.
An old man walks a long way to sit where the road bends. The road remembers him.
Dusk is when the old stories sound true. Come back at dusk some time.
Mind the pack, it bruises.
Two dusks she's been gone. She comes to the smell of it at dusk — if she can.
standingGoodLines: ...Wait. I know your face — the Ranger they talk about, the one creatures come back to.
Ask me again about my Kittember. Talking about her to a kind face is better than not talking.

lines: This is her hour. If she's anywhere, she's deciding right now.
One more dusk. I can do one more dusk. I've done harder maths than hope.
Pupbble! Here, girl — HERE— ...Sorry. She's been gone since the grass rustled at dawn.
She's small, she's quick, and she's TERRIFIED of strangers. Which is everyone, to her, except me.
If she beds down in the deep grass overnight she'll be half-feral by morning. Please. If you see her—
You ever see a grown man cry over a lead rope? You have now. She's HOME.
She sleeps against my boots now. Both of us learned something.
The Plex had a queue out the door this morning. Good. Busy means alive.
Steps are for sitting at dusk. Town rule. Unwritten, enforced by everyone.
